examples.title: Check the contract separately
examples.sql: SELECT json_schema_validate_schema(definition) AS schema_ok FROM contract;

examples.title: Classify every incoming record
examples.sql:
SELECT id, COALESCE(TRY(json_schema_validate(definition, payload)), false) AS valid
FROM incoming CROSS JOIN contract ORDER BY id;

examples.title: Summarize the quality gate
examples.sql:
WITH checked AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(TRY(json_schema_validate(definition, payload)), false) AS valid
  FROM incoming CROSS JOIN contract
)
SELECT count(*) AS received, count(*) FILTER (WHERE valid) AS accepted,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT valid) AS rejected
FROM checked;

sampleSpecs.description: The input is valid JSON or SQL NULL. The contract checks structure and values after JSON parsing.

challenge.title: Keep only valid paid orders
challenge.prompt: Return id for records that satisfy the contract and have status paid. A paid label alone is not enough.
challenge.hint: Combine the validation predicate with the status predicate. Check the contract separately before using TRY on records.
challenge.solution:
SELECT id FROM incoming CROSS JOIN contract
WHERE COALESCE(TRY(json_schema_validate(definition, payload)), false)
  AND payload ->> '$.status' = 'paid'
ORDER BY id;
challenge.success: Only record 1 passes both checks. The other paid records have invalid totals.
